discussion_comments.comment_body:
Partly addressed in `f3d72676` — but the HIGH severity is overstated. These are prose rule-citations ("rule 1", "rule 5"), not backtick-wrapped path tokens, so they do not trip validation: `validate:refs --strict` (220 refs, 0 broken) and `validate:skills --strict` (no findings on this skill) both pass before and after the change. There is also no runtime dead-end — `automation-mode.md` is read once at SKILL.md Step 0 into persistent context, so the step files never re-open it; the citations just name a rule already loaded.

That said, I made them explicit (`../automation-mode.md`) at all three locations (`step-01:15`, `step-03-triage:57`, `step-04-present:15`/`:21`) for consistency with the PATH-05 `deferred-work-format` references and to preempt re-flagging. So the wording is now unambiguous, but to be clear it was not a real validation break.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `9b7db3cc`. Section 6 now reads "Update the spec's YAML frontmatter `status:` field to `done`/`in-progress`" instead of the ambiguous "Status section". This matches automation-mode rule 8 ("frontmatter `status:`"), quick-dev's own step-auto-finalize ("Change `{spec_file}` status in the frontmatter"), and `spec-template.md` (which carries `status:` in YAML, with no markdown "## Status" section). Grounded in the orchestrator: `bmad-auto`'s `verify.py` reads the frontmatter via `read_frontmatter()` and the review gate requires `status == "done"` (`verify_review`, ~L679-682) — a markdown section would have failed that check and burned retries.
